by: party-finance session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at party-finance-1)
title: Electoral Commission: its table of party election expenses for one general election

landmarks: 2023 shape: six cells a row, the party's name as the link to its return, then limit, total expenses, allocation, allocation spent, audit report
2020 shape: seven cells a row (some rows lead with an empty cell), the party's name as plain text, four figures, then a last cell carrying the link

signals_note: An HTML page, so recognition is by structure: one table, a fixed count of figure cells a row per election. A row whose figure cells differ in number is set aside, never guessed into columns.

2023: party (link to the return; an amended row links the amendment, then the original)

notes: The Commission transcribing the returns it links: the outside figure each return's own total is checked against, and a second opinion, not an authority. Its 2020 table prints Part A alone as the total for Advance NZ and the Maori Party, and ACT's total as `$108,2166.64` (digits sound, comma misplaced). NIL is a figure (zero); N/A means no allocation and is no figure. A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: elections.nz party-expenses pages for the 2020 and 2023 general elections, as captured by the old ec-disclosures --party-expenses job under var/staging/ec-donations/index/.

tooling.index: the old estate's ec-disclosures job (headed browser, rulings 242/243)

process: One row is one party's return for one election.
The link text states which linked return is the amendment ('(amended)'); that statement is read, never inferred, and the row's figure belongs to the amendment.
Each link's URL is joined to a held document by the old job's manifest, never by a file name.
gates: Every data row is a listing row or a catch-log line: rows seen equal rows read plus rows set aside.
Every link is a held document or a catch-log line.
on_fail: set aside the row; publish the rest

title: Electoral Commission: its table of registered promoters' election expenses for one general election

landmarks: exactly one <table> on the page, headed 'Registered promoter'
2023 shape: the promoter as the link to its return, then election expenses
2020 shape: the promoter as plain text, then election, cannabis referendum and End of Life Choice Act referendum expenses, then the link

signals_note: An HTML page: recognition by structure, one table and a fixed count of figure cells a row per election.

2020: End of Life Choice Act referendum expenses

notes: Referendum advertising is held beside election advertising and never added to it (facts and traps). Family First New Zealand's 2020 row prints one figure, $141,224.34, in all three columns: kept as printed, a question for its return. A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: elections.nz registered-promoter-expenses pages for the 2020 and 2023 general elections, as captured under var/staging/ec-donations/index/.
process: One row is one registered promoter's return for one election.
Each link's URL is joined to a held document by the old job's manifest.
gates: Every data row is a listing row or a catch-log line.
Every link is a held document or a catch-log line.
on_fail: set aside the row; publish the rest

by: party-finance session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at party-finance-1)
title: Electoral Commission: the broadcasting allocation for one general election, as its page prints it

landmarks: exactly one <table> with one <thead>, one <tbody> and one <tfoot>
the head's first cell 'Political Party', then one cell per round ('Original allocation', each variation)
the foot: 'TOTAL allocated' and 'TOTAL available', one figure per round
the body split by full-width rows: 'Parties eligible for share of broadcasting allocation', 'Parties not eligible for allocation'

signals_note: An HTML page: recognition by structure. The page is the document; it has no asset.
notes: Whole dollars including GST. A blank cell is no allocation in that round, not zero; $0 is printed as $0. A trailing * or ** on a party is the page's footnote mark (2023: * unregistered; ** a component party of Freedoms New Zealand, not separately entitled), kept as printed. The 2023 'TOTAL available' prints $4145,750 for the first variation (comma misplaced, digits sound). Each round's rows add to its printed 'TOTAL allocated' to the dollar on both pages held. A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: elections.nz broadcasting-allocation pages for the 2020 and 2023 general elections, as captured by the old ec-disclosures --broadcasting job under var/staging/ec-broadcasting/.
process: One body row is one party; one cell is that party's allocation in one round.
The last round is the allocation that stood at the election.
gates: Each round's rows add to the page's own 'TOTAL allocated' to the dollar, or no row of the page publishes.
Every body row is an allocation row or a catch-log line.
on_fail: set aside the page; publish nothing from it
